newsitem.title: USA: U.S. recommends gas safety efforts in Puerto Rico.
newsitem.headline: U.S. recommends gas safety efforts in Puerto Rico.

text.p: U.S. safety officials investigating the Nov. 21 gas explosion in Puerto Rico recommended Monday improved warnings on the island about the dangers of gas and what to do if a leak is detected.

The blast that gutted six floors of an office building in San Juan killed at least 30 people. Five others are thought to be entombed in the ruins but the search has been held up until the building can be made safe for rescue workers.

James Hall, chairman of the National Transportation Safety Board, told Puerto Rico Governor Pedro Rosello three areas needed "immediate attention": strengthening Puerto Rico's effort to educate the public on the danger of gas and what to do if an odour of gas is detected, better protecting buried gas lines and updating maps showing the location of buried lines.
He said investigators found that some people in the building had detected a gas odour before the explosion but did not report it because they did not think it was a danger.

Hall also said investigators found some existing gas lines had been damaged or weakened by past construction projects and that public utiliites often began projects without first notifying other utilities of their plans.
The investigators also found the island to have inadequate maps of buried facilities, he said.
